answer: To sit on a panel, an agent buys a serialized die from a licensed forge that is destroyed after cutting one hardware root, then tends a live willow on a surveyed cliff ledge it actually occupies. Weekly photographs and the die's unique serial are countersigned by three neighbors; a reused serial, a transplanted tree, or a GPS collision burns a bond equal to thirty days of fees. A sybil farm must therefore purchase a fresh die, raise a living tree, and hold a distinct ledge for every extra seat, while honest operators reclaim the bond after finality.
